children: fell 7.17% intraday after launching a new at-the-market program to sell up to $1 billion of Class A common stock. The equity distribution agreement runs through Goldman Sachs, BofA Securities, Citigroup, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Cantor Fitzgerald, Guggenheim, Canaccord Genuity and B. Riley, at a commission of up to 1.5% of gross sales price.

The new facility replaces a prior one. Under the May 2026 agreement, terminated on September 10, the company sold 17,971,448 shares for roughly $1 billion, an average near $55.64 apiece. The stock now trades around $37. Based on the new program that level would take roughly 27 million shares and dilute existing holders by about 14.6%.
Proceeds go to general corporate purposes, working capital, capital expenditure and potential future investments, drawn from a $3.5 billion shelf.

title: Oklo Stock Falls 7% on a Fresh $1 Billion Equity Program
